answers.reasoning: Rank loss is singularity. A small positive singular value with full rank is near singular, not exact singularity; a zero entry alone says nothing; a negative nonzero determinant still permits inversion. Square qualification is explicit where needed.

A0=0=lambda0 for every lambda, not only zero. Excluding the zero vector does not change invertibility. diag(0,1) has zero eigenvalue with nonzero eigenvector (1,0); new distractors now express actual eigenvector/eigenvalue confusions.
The explicitly finite absolute first moment makes integral x f_X well-defined and finite. Density integrates to one, peak height is not mean, and an unweighted sum is not expectation.

Interpretability is an object-specific trace of explicit tests to the chosen force. Aggregate accuracy or training information gain does not alone explain this path, and one example does not certify physical safety.

Feasibility and applicability assumptions now explicitly restore the necessary scope. The probability of finding a feasible solution tends to one as time increases without giving finite-run certainty or optimality.

The source permits quick near-optimal results while denying an absolute finite-step shortest-path guarantee. One success proves no universal later outcome; no guarantee is not impossibility; completeness is not optimality.
